maya: Heads-up — proposing a targeted access sweep next week: we'll sample ~10% of admin entitlements across prod orgs, collect owner evidence, and auto-snooze items if an owner responds. Need quick sign-off and a lightweight runbook.

alex: Quick Q — what do you mean by 'admin entitlements'? roles, service accounts, KMS grants, keys?

maya: Short answer: all of the above. Specifically: project/org IAM bindings with admin-ish roles, KMS key bindings, and service-account keys that appear unused or ownerless. We'll limit blast by sampling and dry-run first.

maya: Example queries we'll use:
```
# ownerless svcacct-ish heuristic (gcloud + jq)
gcloud iam service-accounts list --format=json | jq '.[] | select(.displayName==null or .description=="" )'

# check KMS key iam bindings
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy my-key --location=global --keyring=default --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.role | test("roles/.*Admin"))'
```

sam: Audit logs question — do we have 90+ days of admin-change logs to show last-use? For KMS and IAM events?

maya: Yes — admin-audit stream goes to bq.redwood.admin_audit with 180d retention. Cloud Audit -> bigquery for KMS events. We'll join last_authn event to determine last-used time.

olivia: I worry about false positives on infra oncall and CI svcaccts. We should whitelist known infra principals before any action.

jordan: Suggest sampling stratified by principal type: humans 10% sampling, svcaccts 25%. Also stratify by last-used: >90 days unused gets higher sampling weight. Canary plan: collect evidence + notify only; no removal in dry-run.

maya: Agreed. Runbook (draft):
1) run query to produce candidate list + last_used timestamp
2) filter out whitelist file
3) send automated DM + email to detected owner(s) with one-click confirm link
4) wait 7 days for response; if owner requests change, track it
5) escalate to team leads if no response after 7 days
6) after 21 days of no owner evidence, create remediation ticket (manual remove only after manual review)

maya: Notification template draft: "Hi @owner — you are listed as owner of <binding> in project <proj>. Please confirm ownership here: <link> within 7 days. If you don't own it, reply or file SEC ticket and we'll hand to the right team."

alex: Who will run the sweep service? Need to ensure the runner svcacct has least privilege — read-only to audit sources only. No modify perms.

maya: We'll use sec-sweeper@redwood with minimal perms: bigquery.read, iam.roles.list, iam.getPolicy, kms.keys.getIamPolicy. It will not have iam.setPolicy or key versions/crypto permissions. Dry-run flag will be default true.

sam: I'll add a k8s/ops alert mapping so oncall isn't paged for dry-run notifications. Also add a flag to suppress slack DMs for 'infrastructure' owners if listed in the whitelist.

olivia: ✅ Please include the whitelist as a repo-managed yaml and allow rapid edits. Also include an opt-out tag for infra teams.

sec-bot: Created ticket #SEC-4821: "Access sampling sweep — evidence collection". Assignees: maya, sam. ETA: 2026-04-02.

jordan: Timeline looks good. I'll volunteer to draft the Slack DM template and the BigQuery joins for last-authn tomorrow.

maya: Thanks — plan to kick off a small dry-run on 2026-03-30 against a single prod project. tagging @security-leads for awareness :eyes: :lock:

maya: Action items:
- maya: finalize queries + whitelist by 2026-03-26
- sam: add oncall suppress + alert mapping by 2026-03-27
- jordan: DM template + BQ joins by 2026-03-25
- alex: audit svcacct perms for sec-sweeper by 2026-03-28

alex: +1 to timeline. Keep remediation manual for now.

olivia: Thanks — please add me to the SEC-4821 ticket for white-list reviews.

jordan: I'll post the first DM template PR tomorrow AM.

maya: Great — closing this thread for now, will post dry-run results + metrics after 03-30.
